## DayZ

### 1. Is it really self-hostable for a hosting company to resell?

**Independent verdict: the codebase's technical premise is half-right and half-outdated. The "hold a customer's personal Steam credentials" framing is wrong — nobody in this industry does that — but there IS a real, still-unsolved engineering + legal package here that's bigger than just "Steam login."**

- **SteamCMD app ID**: 223350 ("DayZ Server"), confirmed via [SteamDB](https://steamdb.info/app/223350/) and the [LinuxGSM DayZ server page](https://linuxgsm.com/servers/dayzserver/). Linux-native (no Wine needed) — confirmed by LinuxGSM's Linux server support and multiple current Linux Docker projects.
- **Login requirement — verified, still true in 2026**: Community consensus across multiple independent 2026 sources (a live [GitHub issue on steam-for-linux](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/13474) opened specifically about "setting up a dedicated DayZ server on Linux," current SteamCMD guides) confirms: **anonymous SteamCMD login does not reliably work for DayZ's server files, and Steam Workshop mod downloads are always tied to an account that owns DayZ (app 221100)** — not the server app itself. There is some conflicting community chatter that a *vanilla, no-mods* server binary pull can sometimes succeed anonymously, but this is inconsistent and unconfirmed enough that I'm flagging it: **NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING** (test directly: `steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update 223350 validate +quit` against current Steam backend). It's also moot in practice — see below.
- **Why it's moot**: every real competitor I checked (section 8) leads its marketing with Workshop/DZSA mod support, meaning the addressable market overwhelmingly wants modded servers. A Nxeon DayZ product that only works unmodded would not be competitive, so the licensed-account path is required regardless of whether anonymous vanilla-only pulls work.
- **The actual solved mechanism (this is the key finding)**: This is NOT "hold each customer's Steam password + 2FA," and it is NOT "hold Nxeon's own personal gaming account." It's an industry-standard pattern documented directly in [LinuxGSM issue #4117](https://github.com/GameServerManagers/LinuxGSM/issues/4117) and general SteamCMD automation guides: buy **one (or a handful of) dedicated "service" Steam account(s)** that own DayZ, log in **once, interactively**, solve the Steam Guard/2FA challenge that one time, and SteamCMD caches a **sentry file / login token** in the account's local Steam data directory. Every subsequent headless `app_update`/`workshop_download_item` call reuses that cached credential with zero further prompts — this is exactly how LinuxGSM, GameServerManagers, and (per their public marketing pages) Nitrado/GTXGaming/BisectHosting/Shockbyte/Cybrancee all operate DayZ fleets at scale using a small pool of centrally-managed accounts, not per-customer credentials. This is a genuine engineering deliverable for Nxeon (secure storage for one Steam session/sentry-file secret, refreshed if Steam ever invalidates it, plus a runbook for re-solving Steam Guard if it happens) — **but it is a one-time, bounded, solvable piece of work, not the open-ended "no platform mechanism exists" blocker the codebase describes.** I'd characterize the codebase's comment as **stale as of Sept 2026** on the credentials point specifically.
- **A second, previously-unflagged blocker that's arguably bigger**: DayZ is configured via **command-line launch parameters and a `serverDZ.cfg` text file**, not Docker environment variables the way CS2/Rust/V Rising are. The one community Docker image I could inspect in detail ([mr-guard/dayz-sa-server-docker](https://github.com/mr-guard/dayz-sa-server-docker)) only exposes generic envs (`STEAM_CMD_USER`, `STEAM_CMD_PASSWORD`, `UPDATE_EXTRA_ARGS`, `START_EXTRA_ARGS`, `APP_ID`) — there is no `SERVER_NAME`/`SERVER_PASSWORD`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD`-style per-field env surface at all. That means Nxeon's `envKey`-per-field schema pattern doesn't map cleanly onto DayZ; the provisioning worker would need a **config-file templating step** (writing `serverDZ.cfg` contents at deploy time) in addition to, or instead of, env-var substitution. This is real net-new plumbing, separate from the credentials problem.
- **Legal/EULA caveat (new finding, not in the codebase at all)**: I fetched the [Steam EULA for app 223350](https://store.steampowered.com/eula/223350_eula_0) directly. It states plainly: *"You may use the software for non-commercial purposes only,"* *"Do not use the software... commercially without Our permission,"* and *"You must not redistribute, publish, license, rent or resell the software... without Our permission."* Read literally, this bars exactly what Nxeon would be doing. In practice this text is boilerplate that the entire game-hosting industry treats as unenforced/normalized (dozens of commercial hosts sell DayZ, Valheim, Palworld, etc. under near-identical language, with no known enforcement action against hosts), but it is a real, distinct risk from the technical blocker, and worth an explicit sign-off from Nxeon's owner rather than assuming it's fine because "everyone else does it."

**Bottom line on viability**: the pure technical blocker as described in the codebase is **outdated/overstated** — real hosts solve it with a small pool of service accounts + cached session tokens, which Nxeon could replicate. What's still open is (a) the config-file-vs-env-var engineering gap, and (b) an EULA commercial-use clause that the whole industry quietns around but nobody has cleared. I'd change the internal status from "blocked — no mechanism exists" to **"blocked pending an engineering spike (service-account credential storage + config templating) and an explicit owner decision on the EULA risk," not an unsolvable wall.**

### 2. The real Docker image to use

No single image is both (a) actively maintained with recent commits and (b) has a fully-documented, complete env-var surface. Candidates found:
- `mr-guard/dayz-sa-server-docker` — has the clearest Steam-login env vars (`STEAM_CMD_USER`, `STEAM_CMD_PASSWORD`) and Workshop support via `UPDATE_EXTRA_ARGS`, but sparse/undocumented server-config exposure. Commit recency **NEEDS VERIFICATION** (page only showed "2 Commits," no dates surfaced).
- `anthony-mariotti/docker-dayz-server` — configurable, but explicitly vanilla/no-mods only per its own description, which conflicts with the modded-demand finding in §1/§8.
- `icedream/docker-dayzserver` — labeled by its own author as "WIP and highly experimental."
- `fantwings/dayz-exp-server` — exists on Docker Hub; not independently vetted here.

**NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING**: none of these should be trusted as production-grade without directly opening each Dockerfile/entrypoint and confirming (1) recent commit activity, (2) exact env-to-config-file mapping, (3) Workshop mod handling. This is a real gap relative to CS2's `joedwards32/cs2`, which is a known, singular, well-adopted image — DayZ has no equivalent community consensus image.

### 3. Environment variables / config mechanism

- Steam auth: `STEAM_CMD_USER` / `STEAM_CMD_PASSWORD` (per mr-guard image) pointing at Nxeon's own service account, **never** a per-customer field.
- Server identity/behavior: **not** environment-variable driven in the vanilla binary — driven by CLI params (`-config=`, `-port=`, `-profiles=`, `-mod=`, `-BEpath=`) and the contents of `serverDZ.cfg` (hostname, password, maxPlayers, etc.) plus BattlEye's `BEServer_x64.cfg` (`RConPassword`, `RConPort`). Confirmed via [Bohemia's own DayZ:Server_Configuration wiki](https://community.bistudio.com/wiki/DayZ:Server_Configuration) (referenced, not directly fetchable — got a 403) and corroborated by third-party guides (MantaScope, RespawnHost).
- **Everything customer-facing needs to go through config-file templating, not `envKey` substitution.** This is the single most important schema-shape mismatch to flag.

### 4. Ports

- Game port: **2302/UDP** (confirmed by multiple current hosting docs, e.g. RedSwitches, LOW.MS).
- Steam query port: **2303/UDP** (game port + 1) — "has no reliable cross-source default; set explicitly," per community guidance, so don't hardcode blindly.
- BattlEye RCon port: **recommended game port + 3 (2305/UDP by default)**, must be explicitly configured and kept outside the 2302–2306 range to avoid collisions — confirmed via [Bohemia's Feedback Tracker T159179](https://feedback.bistudio.com/T159179) and BattlEye-Extended-Controls project notes.
- All of this is **UDP**, no TCP surface exists for health-checking. For `GAME_PORT`, use `{ port: 2302, protocol: "udp" }`.

### 5. Draft FamilySchema (framed as "if the licensing blocker is solved")

```ts
{
  family: "dayz",
  label: "DayZ",
  variants: [
    { id: "vanilla", label: "Vanilla", description: "No mods, official maps only" },
    { id: "modded", label: "Modded (Workshop)", description: "Requires Nxeon-owned Steam service account; NEEDS VERIFICATION on Workshop automation reliability" },
  ],
  defaultVariant: "vanilla",
  fields: [
    { key: "serverName", label: "Server Name", group: "General", type: "string", default: "Nxeon DayZ Server", phase: "deploy", required: true,
      help: "Written into serverDZ.cfg (hostname) — NOT a docker env var; requires config-file templating, not envKey substitution. NEEDS VERIFICATION." },
    { key: "serverPassword", label: "Join Password", group: "General", type: "string", default: "", phase: "deploy",
      help: "serverDZ.cfg 'password' field. Left blank in setupScript; substituted at provision time like RCON secrets are for palworld/rust/cs2." },
    { key: "rconPassword", label: "Admin (RCon) Password", group: "Admin", type: "string", default: "", phase: "deploy", required: true,
      help: "BattlEye RConPassword in BEServer_x64.cfg — a DIFFERENT proprietary protocol from Source RCON. Needs applyGameControlSecrets support added for this family; does not exist yet." },
    { key: "maxPlayers", label: "Max Players", group: "General", type: "int", default: 60, min: 1, max: 120, phase: "deploy",
      help: "serverDZ.cfg 'maxPlayers'. Typical community servers run 40-80; NEEDS VERIFICATION on any hard engine ceiling." },
    { key: "map", label: "Map", group: "General", type: "enum", default: "chernarusplus", phase: "deploy",
      options: [
        { value: "chernarusplus", label: "Chernarus" },
        { value: "enoch", label: "Livonia" },
        { value: "namalsk", label: "Namalsk (mod map)" },
        { value: "sakhal", label: "Sakhal" },
      ] },
    { key: "thirdPerson", label: "Allow Third-Person View", group: "Gameplay", type: "bool", default: true, phase: "deploy" },
    { key: "workshopModIds", label: "Workshop Mod IDs (comma-separated)", group: "Mods", type: "string", default: "", phase: "deploy",
      help: "Requires the Nxeon service Steam account to own/subscribe these; each mod ID pulled via `+workshop_download_item 221100 <id>`. NEEDS VERIFICATION on reliability/timeouts at scale." },
  ],
}
```

### 6. Draft setupScript (speculative — engineering spike required before this is real)

```
"curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name dayz -p 2302:2302/udp -p 2303:2303/udp -p 2305:2305/udp -v /opt/dayz:/home/steam/dayz-server -e STEAM_CMD_USER='NXEON_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PLACEHOLDER' -e STEAM_CMD_PASSWORD='' -e SERVER_NAME='' -e SERVER_PASSWORD='' -e RCON_PASSWORD='changeme' --restart unless-stopped mr-guard/dayz-sa-server-docker:latest"
```
**Caveats on this draft, explicitly**: (1) the image's real env surface for `SERVER_NAME`/`SERVER_PASSWORD`/`RCON_PASSWORD` is **unconfirmed** — the README excerpt I could retrieve did not document these; they may not exist and may require mounting a pre-rendered `serverDZ.cfg`/`BEServer_x64.cfg` instead. (2) `STEAM_CMD_USER`/`PASSWORD` must point at Nxeon's own service account credential store, never left blank/customer-supplied. This entire script is **NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING** — do not copy into `lib/games.ts` without first standing up a real test container and confirming behavior.

### 7. Resource sizing

DayZ is heavy — among the heaviest games in the whole "likely to add" batch. Real competitor tiers (Cybrancee, §8) start at **8GB RAM** and go up:

| Tier | RAM | CPU | Disk | Slots | Nxeon Plan mapping |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small | 8192 MB | 3 cores | 40 GB | ~30 | **Pro** (8192MB/3cpu) — exact fit |

## CS 1.6

### 1. Is it really self-hostable for a hosting company to resell?

Yes, cleanly — this is a much simpler, better-understood case than DayZ. Confirmed:
- **SteamCMD app ID 90** ("hlds" / Half-Life Dedicated Server), Linux-native, **anonymous login works** — there is no ownership/licensing gate on this appid at all (it's Valve's classic free-to-download dedicated server tool, pre-dating any GSLT/licensed-account requirements). No EULA commercial-resale red flag was found for HLDS/CS1.6 (unlike DayZ's explicit non-commercial clause) — this is the same free public-dedicated-server model every other family in Nxeon's catalog already uses via anonymous SteamCMD.
- **A known, long-standing, still-current quirk**: appid 90 has a well-documented bug where the **first `app_update 90 validate` run downloads a stale/wrong appmanifest and only pulls a partial install (30-70MB)**; you must re-run the same command (sometimes 2-3×) until it reports "App successfully updated!" This is described across multiple sources as a persistent, years-old, **still-unresolved-as-of-2026** issue, not something new — confirmed via current [Steam Community discussions](https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/16/1369506834138679429/) and forum threads. **Any setupScript for this family must loop `app_update 90 validate` at least twice, unconditionally** — this is a concrete, verified quirk to bake into automation, not a guess.
- No GSLT (Game Server Login Token) requirement — confirmed via multiple sources: GSLT was introduced for **Source-engine-and-later** titles (CS:GO/CSS, later CS2) around the CS:GO era; it does not apply to GoldSrc/HLDS/appid 90. This directly confirms the prompt's hint: **CS 1.6 does NOT need a GSLT/SRCDS_TOKEN the way CS2 does** — that requirement is Source-engine-specific and postdates GoldSrc's design.

### 2. The real Docker image to use

Several actively-referenced community images combine HLDS + Metamod + AMXX + fastdownload:
- **`archont94/counter-strike1.6`** (Docker Hub + GitHub, MIT license) — the best-documented candidate found. README confirms it bundles Metamod + AMX Mod X + a fast-download HTTP asset server (port 80), with a clean, small env-var surface (§3). Commit count shown as 12; **exact last-commit date could not be confirmed via the fetch tool — NEEDS VERIFICATION on "actively maintained" before committing to it** (check `git log` / GitHub API directly rather than trusting a page summary).
- **`vitordino/counter-strike-docker`** — advertises "raw Steam HLDS + Metamod + DProto + AMX MOD X," also supports a hybrid Steam/no-Steam mode (not relevant to Nxeon, which should stay Steam-authenticated for legitimacy/anti-cheat compatibility).
- **`hpoon/HLDS-CS1.6`**, **`kran0/hlds-docker`**, **`cajuclc/cstrike-docker`** — older/smaller community projects, bundle Metamod+AMXX+bots (Podbot); maintenance activity not verified, treat as fallback options only.
- **Pterodactyl "Counter-Strike 1.6 - ReHLDS" egg** ([eggs.pterodactyl.io](https://eggs.pterodactyl.io/egg/games-counter-strike-1-6-rehlds/)) — uses `ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/games:source`, runs **ReHLDS** (a modern, actively-maintained reverse-engineered replacement for the original HLDS binary — [github.com/rehlds](https://github.com/rehlds), with its ReGameDLL_CS component showing a mirror sync as recently as **2026-05-30**, confirming the broader engine-modernization ecosystem is genuinely alive in 2026, not abandoned). This egg confirms plugin support is designed in ("Advanced scripting platform for server plugins" = Metamod/AMXX).

**Recommendation**: prefer **ReHLDS over vanilla HLDS** as the engine binary if building a custom Nxeon image (better stability/security/performance per its own docs), layered with Metamod + AMX Mod X — but there is no single dominant, unambiguously-current turnkey image the way `joedwards32/cs2` is for CS2. **NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING**: pick `archont94/counter-strike1.6` or build in-house on top of ReHLDS, and confirm actual recent commit activity before locking it in.

### 3. Environment variables / config mechanism

From the `archont94/counter-strike1.6` README (directly fetched, verbatim-sourced):
- `PORT` (default 27015)
- `MAP` (default de_dust2)
- `MAXPLAYERS` (default 16)
- `SV_LAN` (default 0)
- `SERVER_NAME` (default "Counter-Strike 1.6 DockerServer")
- `FAST_DL` (default "http://127.0.0.1/cstrike/")
- `ADMIN_STEAM_ID` (default "STEAM_0:0:123456" — for AMXX admin recognition)

**Important, verified gotcha — exactly the V Rising bug class this task is designed to catch**: this image's real env vars are **UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and do not match a natural camelCase schema `key`** (e.g. `key: "serverName"` vs actual env `SERVER_NAME`; `key: "maxPlayers"` vs `MAXPLAYERS`). **Every single field needs an explicit `envKey`** — if Nxeon ships this family without setting `envKey` on each field, it will silently break exactly the way V Rising did.
- **RCON password is notably absent from this image's documented env vars.** The README explicitly says *"the server.cfg file can override the settings from your environment variables"* — meaning RCON password (`rcon_password` in GoldSrc's `server.cfg`) is **not exposed as a docker env var in this image at all**; it must be injected via a mounted/templated `server.cfg` file, similar to the DayZ config-file gotcha (smaller in scope here — just the one field). **Flag as NEEDS VERIFICATION**: either extend the image to accept an `RCON_PASSWORD` env, or have Nxeon's worker write `server.cfg` at provision time.

### 4. Ports

- **27015** — game port, **UDP** (confirmed via the image's own `docker run` example and general GoldSrc knowledge; the same example also publishes 27015/TCP, but this appears to be Dockerfile boilerplate/cargo-culting rather than a real listener — GoldSrc's actual game protocol, including A2S queries, is UDP-only, same as CS2's own port entry which is UDP despite being a different engine generation).
- **80** — HTTP, used only for the fast-download asset server (maps/sprays), not part of the game protocol itself.
- **RCON** — GoldSrc RCON is a **legacy UDP challenge-response protocol** (`rcon_password` + `challenge` handshake), served on the same UDP port as the game (27015), not a separate port.
- For `GAME_PORT`: `{ port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }` — same shape as CS2's entry, appropriate for post-boot A2S health checks.

CS 1.6/GoldSrc is a 2003-era engine — by a wide margin the lightest game under consideration. Real competitor pricing (GHOSTCAP: "$3-10/month depending on player slots") confirms this.

| Tier | RAM | CPU | Disk | Slots | Nxeon Plan mapping |

| Small | 512-1024 MB | 1 core | 5 GB | 12-16 | **Nano** (1024MB/1cpu) — comfortable fit, likely oversized even |

CS 1.6 would be the **only family that fits entirely within Nxeon's two smallest Plan tiers (Nano/Starter)** — genuinely the cheapest possible catalog slot, which is a real differentiator vs. DayZ needing Pro/Max.
